sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties
Luxembourg Double Taxation Treaties with the Netherlands, France, and the United States
EU–Republic of China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (as applicable)
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the implementation of the beneficial ownership register; CSSF Regulation No 12/02 and associated CSSF AML/CFT circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (statuts) approving the corporate name and registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial deed executed by an admitted Luxembourg notary; no consular legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and certificate of incumbency for any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade and Companies Register of the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the origin country is not a party to the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card copies of all ultimate beneficial owners and proposed managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport / civil registry authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarially certified copy or apostilled copy subject to the country of issuance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against PEP, OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU autonomous sanctions, and Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (MROS) warnings. Source-of-funds evidence must be retained for any capital contribution. Continuous AML/CFT monitoring applies under CSSF and Law of 12 November 2004 protocols.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be comprehensible in Luxembourgish, French, or German and may use internationally accepted Latin transliteration for foreign words. The name must not be misleading as to the company's legal form and must include the statutory suffix 'SARL'. It must be sufficiently distinctive and must not create a likelihood of confusion with any existing RCS entry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission de surveillance du secteur financier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a fresh name-availability request through the LBR portal or apply for review by the director of the RCS. Where ministerial authorization is refused (e.g., for banking or insurance tokens), an administrative appeal must be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of written notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through an approved domiciliation service provider; a pure virtual mailbox or post-office box without local administrative substance is inadmissible. The SARL must maintain a real registered address and an operational base proportionate to its stated engineering and BIM outsourcing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<10%) for a non-PEP, standard-risk engineering CAD/BIM outsourcing entity, but unannounced inspections can be triggered by irregular domiciliation, absence of UBO updates, or unusual wire transfer patterns during the first two years after incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name availability check and statutory name clearance search via LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Non-chargable portal service; independent legal search recommended at hourly rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence, AML/CDD review and drafting of incorporation instructions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 300–500 per hour; fixed fee acceptable for simple SARL structures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (statuts) including notarial authentication of all founder signature pages
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Luxembourg notarial tariff scale based on registered capital and deed volume

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the corporate founder's registration documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Luxembourg or the origin state's competent apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fixed fee (approximately EUR 20 per document) plus expediting and courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate registry documents into French, German, or English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg District Court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document/page, typically EUR 80–150 per standard company form

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office and domiciliation service prepayment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual rate EUR 1,200–1,800 depending on substance and mail-forwarding requirements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-26 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on annual accounts of undertakings, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 7 rue Alcide de Gasperi, L-2981 Luxembourg; incorporation filings are submitted electronically by the notary via the LBR portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution / statuts) executed before a Luxembourg notary, filed electronically with the RCS, and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; each quota must have a par value of at least EUR 1. Cash contributions must be deposited before notarisation into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the company in formation ('S.à r.l. en formation') with a Luxembourg credit institution, and the bank's blocking certificate must be presented to the notary; funds are released only upon RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a report by a Luxembourg-approved auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and paid up in accordance with Article 710-6 of the Law of 10 August 1915, the bank blocking certificate being tabled and approved; (2) that the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles of association and the manager is authorised to record it with the Luxembourg Business Registers; (3) that [Name] is appointed first manager (gérant) with sole signature power, effective upon registration; (4) that the notary be instructed to execute the notarial deed and complete the RCS filing and RESA publication; (5) that all post-registration formalities, including VAT and Chamber of Commerce enrolment, are delegated to the manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online name search and booking portal (lbr.lu / guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS-registered names via the free LBR name search; optionally book the name for a renewable two-month period so the notary can finalise the deed with guaranteed availability. Confirm that the name contains the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the acronym 'S.à r.l.' and does not infringe registered trademarks; obtain the LBR name availability receipt.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to four variants)
Summary statement of corporate objects (ISIC 7110 – BIM/CAD engineering services)
Identification of the intended shareholder(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, refile immediately with the next variant or lodge a written contestation with the RCS registrar; the notary adjusts the deed accordingly at no substantive cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked share-capital account (compte bloqué) and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas, ING Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles of association and full KYC file to the chosen Luxembourg bank, transfer the EUR 12,000 minimum capital to the account opened in the name of 'S.à r.l. en formation', and instruct the bank to issue the blocking certificate (certificat de blocage) confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the company to be formed; the certificate must be addressed to the notary and dated not older than the signing day.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Passport copies of all shareholders and managers
Proof of residential address (utility bill or equivalent)
Bank KYC/AML forms including source of wealth and source of funds declarations
Business plan and target market description for the offshore BIM/CAD services
For corporate shareholders: certificate of incorporation, registry extracts, board resolution and ultimate beneficial owner identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank serves supplementary KYC requests, deliver the requested source-of-funds evidence within five business days; if approval is denied, open the account at an alternative Luxembourg bank and obtain a new blocking certificate; the notary may, at his discretion, accept a blocking confirmation issued through a Luxembourg branch of an EU credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the incorporation deed (acte de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the statuts (name, registered office, corporate objects, EUR 12,000 capital split into quotas with a par value of at least EUR 1 each, manager identity). The notary verifies the blocking certificate, the shareholders' subscription list, the managers' declarations on honour (no bankruptcy, no prohibition to manage) and the registered-office lease consent, then reads and signs the deed with the subscribers (in person or by proxy). The company does not yet exist as a legal person until RCS registration; the notary represents the company in formation for pre-registration steps.
required_dossiers: Final approved articles of association (statuts)
Bank blocking certificate (original)
Share subscription list and payment evidence
Managers' declaration on honour and certificate of no bankruptcy
Consent of the registered office premises owner
Identification documents of all subscribers and proxies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any element (e.g. defective capital wording or missing consent), the subscribers provide corrective documents within 48 hours and the signing is rescheduled; incomplete KYC is cured by fresh supporting evidence acceptable to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and RESA publication by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the LBR e-filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarial deed electronically with the RCS within days of signature. The RCS reviews the file; upon approval the company is assigned an RCS number and is registered, thereby conferring legal personality; the deed and statutory excerpts are published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). The bank releases the blocked capital upon production of the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (electronic deposit)
LBR registration form (submitted by the notary)
Proof of payment of the RCS registration duty (EUR 75)
Annexes required by the RCS registrar (manager acceptance, registered office consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or an observation, the notary files the corrective instrument (acte rectificatif) or missing annexes within the registrar's deadline; if registration is refused, cure the legal defect, sign a corrective deed and refile. The company lacks legal personality until registration, so pre-registration acts must be ratified after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, VAT and Chamber of Commerce formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Chambre de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS extract, the manager files the mandatory VAT registration with the AEDT to obtain the national VAT number (LU...), enrols the company with the Chambre de Commerce (compulsory commercial registration), and registers as an employer with the CCSS if payroll is established; set up the corporate income tax and net wealth tax files with the AEDT for the annual cycle.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarial articles of association
Identification of manager and shareholders
Proof of registered office and banking details
Activity description (ISIC 7110 – engineering CAD/BIM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings are cured by immediate submission with an explanatory letter; late-filing penalties are minimised by voluntary disclosure; the VAT number is issued retroactively to the registration date, and invoices issued in the interim must be regularised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, fire-safety and environmental compliance of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Administration de la Sécurité Incendie et de Secours (SIS); Commune of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the leased offices carry a valid building occupancy certificate; obtain a fire-safety notice from the SIS (first visit), submit an occupational risk assessment to the ITM (workstation ergonomics, electrical installations, safety delegate designation when staff exceed legal thresholds), and confirm waste and wastewater collection arrangements with the commune. Offshore CAD/BIM services have no industrial emissions, no EIA duty and no discharge permit.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement with occupancy/structural certificate
SIS fire-safety application and building plans
ITM workplace risk assessment form
Electrical installation certificate of the landlord
Waste collection contract and communal sewerage conformity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIS or ITM notices deficiencies, implement remedial measures (extinguishers, signage, evacuation plan, electrical re-certification) and request a reinspection; temporary occupancy may be maintained under a written commitment schedule approved by the ITM.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de l'industrie et des PME (Luxembourg); relevant only where on-site engineering consultancy is rendered in Luxembourg, in which case a business establishment authorisation under the Law of 2 September 2011 may be required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – offshore BIM/CAD drafting and structural drawing services are unregulated back-office activities; no industrial operating permit, manufacturing licence or professional card is required for this ISIC 7110 scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure office-based services; the activity is not listed in the annexes to the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA report, registration or scoping opinion required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC/combustion emissions; sanitary wastewater to municipal sewer per communal bylaw; office WEEE and IT waste routed to certified recyclers under the transposition of Directive 2012/19/EU (Law of 21 March 2012); noise limited to 65 dB(A) boundary equivalent; no GHG thresholds applicable to this office activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SIS fire-safety approval (avis de sécurité incendie) for office occupancy; ITM workplace clearance under the Law of 17 June 1994 (risk assessment, electrical installation certificate, safety delegate at legal thresholds); structural load and building compliance borne by the landlord's occupancy certificate issued by the commune; evacuation plan and annual fire drills mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg operates a unitary national tax system with two administrative arms under the Ministry of Finance: (1) Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax, with electronic filing through the eCDF portal; (2) Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and stamp duties. Company registration and corporate data are handled by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS), accessible through the national e-government portal Guichet.lu (MyGuichet).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A resident SARL obtains its tax identity in three steps: (1) notarial deed of incorporation filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), triggering publication in RESA and issuance of the national business register number (matricule) and RCS number; (2) the ACD automatically opens the corporate income tax and municipal business tax file upon RCS notification, issuing the company's direct tax identification number; (3) VAT registration is applied for with the AEDT using form 645 (submitted electronically via MyGuichet or the eCDF business portal), attaching the deed, matricule/RCS extract, business activity description and identification of the gérant; the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number in the format LU + 8 digits, generally within one to four weeks. Foreign entities without a Luxembourg establishment that make taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly for VAT with the AEDT before the first supply (no turnover threshold applies to non-residents) and may be required to appoint a VAT representative approved by the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Luxembourg SARL is an opaque, resident legal entity taxed at entity level; it is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax and net wealth tax on its worldwide income and net wealth, with relief limited to statutory mechanisms such as the participation exemption and tax treaty credits. The SARL has no pass-through status for Luxembourg tax purposes and cannot elect transparency; it is fully taxable in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections and mechanisms relevant to a Luxembourg SARL include: (i) fiscal unity for corporate income tax under Article 164bis LIR, available where a resident parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary, filed with the ACD; (ii) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) with prior AEDT approval, allowing related Luxembourg-established entities to be treated as one VAT taxable person; (iii) written application to the AEDT under the 'use and enjoyment' rule to reallocate the place of supply of certain services effectively consumed outside the EU; (iv) EORI registration to support customs export zero-rating; (v) statutory participation exemption relief, verified at assessment upon meeting the 10% equity threshold and 12-month minimum holding period rather than by election; and (vi) ATAD hybrid mismatch reporting obligations under the cross-border tax rulings framework, with no elective hybrid relief available.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in cooperation with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for balance-of-payments statistics and EU capital-movement oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current and capital account transactions as a consequence of Luxembourg's EU membership and eurozone participation. No prior foreign-exchange authorization is required for profit remittances, capital injections, or trade settlements. Obligations include statistical reporting and sanctions screening, not convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratios apply to export proceeds. Receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be retained, deployed, or remitted without conversion. Cash-based exports above EUR 10,000 trigger the EU cash movement declaration regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – CSSF-licensed or EU-passported payment institutions/e-money institutions are legally viable for operational disbursements and trade settlements; however, full credit institutions are required for statutory capital escrow and any balance-sheet cash holding. A non-EU EMI without passporting presents heightened KYC and tax-transparency challenges.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Initial KYC interview generally requires the physical presence of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) (or a mandate holder) at the Luxembourg bank branch. Remote video verification is increasingly accepted under CSSF guidance upon production of notarized corporate documents, but bank policies remain heterogeneous; notarized signature specimens and board resolutions are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through multi-layered holding or domicile in tax-haven jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified company registry extract, notarized founding documents, full shareholder register, UBO declarations under Luxembourg law (CSSF circular 12/02), economic-substance evidence, and a chronological corporate ownership scheme

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between contract scope, VAT invoicing, and transaction cadence for CAD/BIM deliverables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engineering subcontracts, detailed BIM/CAD scope-of-work statements, interim milestone reports, final acceptance certificates, and reconciled accounting ledger extracts with invoice-to-proceeds mapping

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or repetitive wire transfers to non-EU suppliers linked to infrastructure-components procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade-contract dossier, supplier due-diligence questionnaires, sanctions/PEP screening evidence, pro-forma invoices, bill-of-lading/customs evidence, and an authorized-compliance-attestation from the designated compliance office

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from parent shareholders must be made via SWIFT MT103 wire referencing the statutory purpose code for subscription/payment of share capital and the notarized deed of contribution. The receiving Luxembourg bank credits the capital escrow account only after verification against the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) registration extract and UBO file; the BCL balance-of-payments report and the CSSF statistical return capture the inflow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR-denominated disbursements within the eurozone are executed over the SEPA Credit Transfer system. Cross-border disbursements use SWIFT MT103 with structured remittance information; infrastructure procurement trade settlements may be supported by documentary credits (UCP600), with the issuing bank transferring euro cover through TARGET2 or correspondent accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with credit support annex

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the underlying currency is not fully convertible (e.g., emerging-market infrastructure supply currencies), executed via a licensed Luxembourg or EU investment firm
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term USD/EUR project financing, subject to EMIR reporting and mandatory clearing if applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, notes) and, where applicable, the management report and statutory audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice / eCDF electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of each financial year (e.g., by 30 September for a 31 December year-end); an extension may be requested on justified grounds only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers RCS late-deposit penalties (commonly EUR 100–250), possible court summons with fines of up to EUR 5,000 against directors, and administrative strike-off from the commercial register if the entity remains in default for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Service de taxation des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June following the tax year for paper returns; electronic filing deadlines are commonly extended to 31 December of the same calendar year; the ACD annual communication states the current deadline for each assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% to 20% administrative penalty on the net tax due, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and provisional ex officio assessment (imposition d'office) with a further 10% penalty; deliberate misstatement may expose directors to criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation declaration (confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March of each calendar year, reflecting the position at 31 December of the preceding year; changes in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per violation, with further recurring monthly fines for continuing non-compliance; intentional false declarations are punishable by criminal fines (EUR 750–25,000) and repeated breaches can be used by the RCS as evidence of absence from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory for a Luxembourg SARL when, on the balance-sheet date, the company exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: (i) balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; (ii) net turnover EUR 8,800,000; (iii) average workforce of 50 full-time employees. An audit may also be required at the request of shareholders holding at least 25% of the share capital, by judicial order, or under special sectoral rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Standalone SARL financial statements are prepared under Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and annual accounts, implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; consolidated financial statements may use IFRS for listed and internationally active groups, but statutory annual accounts of the legal entity remain on Lux GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year by 31 March, the SARL must electronically confirm to the Luxembourg RBE that its registered beneficial-ownership data remains accurate as at 31 December. Any shareholding transfer or change of control altering direct or indirect ownership percentages must be filed within 30 days, and the same data must be mirrored contemporaneously in the statutory register of members and minutes. The annual confirmation is required even if no change occurred during the prior year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500–US$3,800 per year for a professional Luxembourg registered office / corporate secretarial agent (dependent on service scope, transaction volume, and mail handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$12,000 per year for a statutory audit engagement of a compact engineering/CAD-BIM SARL, varying with group structure, intercompany balances, and audit depth required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17% Corporate Income Tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% Municipal Business Tax); base CIT rate is 17%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime granting an 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income (effective rate approximately 4.98%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; research and development tax credit up to 13% on eligible R&D expenditures; investment tax credit (crédit d'impôt investissement) for eligible new productive assets; 17-year loss carryforward mitigates effective tax over the project lifecycle

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 600 (Déclaration collective pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) filed electronically via the eCDF portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD), accessible at https://ecdf.public.lu; secondary access via MyGuichet
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Form 600 return must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; for a SARL with fiscal year ending 31 December 2024, the filing deadline is 31 December 2025; the ACD may grant an extension only upon substantiated written request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCIN and RCSL registration number, legal form (SARL), registered office and taxpayer identification data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must use the PE registration number and local PE address; companies without a PE cannot file Form 600

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year commencement and closing dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE accounting period exactly as reflected in the statutory accounts; a non-calendar-year cycle must be pre-approved by the ACD

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of statutory accounts, balance sheet and profit or loss by category of income (engineering services, BIM model development, CAD drafting, project management)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, only the Luxembourg-sourced and PE-attributable profit is declared under OECD Article 7 attribution principles

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (résultat fiscal) after commercial law adjustments, tax provisions and extraordinary items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must add back head-office charges that are not recreating the PE profit; only deductible expenses actually supporting the Luxembourg activity are allowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of losses carried forward (pertes reportables) with attachment of the supporting loss carryforward schedule (17-year rule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE may deduct losses previously incurred by that same PE in Luxembourg; losses of the foreign head office are not attributable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) base, including add-backs of interest and royalty payments exceeding EUR 100,000 and apportionment factors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs apportion the municipal business tax base using Luxembourg payroll and fixed-asset factors in accordance with article 159 of the LIR

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) declaration at 0.5% on taxable net assets, with participation exemption claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARLs declare only Luxembourg-situs assets and PE assets; foreign participations are covered by the aggregate participation exemption

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains, evidencing the 10% shareholding and 12-month holding condition
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate shareholders must attach the parent company's TRC and documentation proving the minimum shareholding and holding period to support reduced DTA rates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP Box computation (80% exemption) with eligible IP rights and nexus-ratio calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may only apply the IP Box on patents, software copyrights and other qualifying IP actually developed by the PE under the nexus approach

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure and summary of intercompany transactions, including the Master File/Local File reference number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs must report intercompany agreements with the head office and related parties exceeding the de minimis thresholds; the documentation must be filed upon ACD request

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of EUR 25 to EUR 25,000; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month on the unpaid tax; the ACD may issue a forced assessment (taxation d'office) disregarding advantageous elections, impose a 10% tax surcharge, and refer intentional non-filing for criminal tax fraud prosecution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions by a resident SARL; fully exempt (0%) under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying corporate shareholder holding at least 10% for at least 12 months; resident corporate shareholders with a 10% participation also benefit from the domestic exemption
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the paying SARL before distribution: (i) a certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's residence state, (ii) a signed beneficial-ownership declaration confirming that no intermediary or artificial arrangement is interposed, (iii) evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period, and (iv) a copy of the DTA article relied upon; the SARL must keep this documentation for at least 10 years. If 15% WHT is withheld in error, the non-resident shareholder must file a refund application (demande en restitution) with the ACD within the five-year statutory limitation period running from 1 January of the year following the levying of the tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties or outbound interest paid by a resident SARL to non-residents, subject to anti-abuse verification; under Luxembourg's DTA network, treaty rates for royalties are commonly 0% or 5% (occasionally 10%) and for interest 0% or 10%, but because no domestic source tax exists, the treaty rates are generally not applied at source; payments must still satisfy the economic substance and beneficial-ownership requirements

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File threshold: the Luxembourg SARL belongs to a group with consolidated annual turnover of at least EUR 50,000,000 and has intercompany transactions exceeding: EUR 1,000,000 for goods, EUR 100,000 for services, EUR 100,000 for financial transactions, or EUR 100,000 for royalties/intangible transactions; Master File threshold: group consolidated turnover of at least EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report threshold: group consolidated turnover of at least EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no sectoral ESR code, but substance is enforceable through the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework standards, the general anti-abuse rule in Article 6 of the Luxembourg Abgabenordnung, the ATAD interest-limitation and CFC rules, Luxembourg administrative circulars on tax residence, and the proposed EU Unshell Directive. For a civil infrastructure CAD/BIM outsourcing SARL, substance is demonstrated by a local registered office, locally resident and technically qualified staff managing the BIM contracts, genuine board and management decision-making in Luxembourg, and arm's-length service agreements; failure to evidence substance triggers recharacterization, denial of DTA/participation-exemption benefits, retroactive 15% withholding, and potential involuntary liquidation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraud (fraude fiscale / escroquerie fiscale)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing false Form 600 declarations, omitting invoiced BIM/CAD revenue, fabricating subcontractor invoices, recording fictitious expenses, destroying accounting records, or disguising dividend distributions as engineering service fees to shift profit to a foreign shareholder
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine between EUR 25,000 and EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years for simple tax fraud; aggravated tax swindle (escroquerie fiscale) carries imprisonment from 1 to 10 years and fines up to EUR 500,000; additionally the ACD reopens the assessment, claims the underpaid tax plus 0.6% monthly interest, and denies all deductions related to the concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal and de facto directors who authorize or conceal false filings are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under the theory of faute grave et caractéristique; directors face criminal conviction, civil restitution of the evaded tax, confiscation orders, travel bans (interdiction de sortir du territoire), and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a letterbox office with zero operational substance, no local employees performing BIM/CAD work, all decisions taken remotely by the foreign shareholder, no local board meetings, and no physical or technical capacity to perform the engineering drafting services for which the SARL invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the general anti-abuse rule reclassifying the SARL as fiscally non-transparent and abusive, denial of treaty benefits and the participation exemption, recapture of the 15% dividend WHT, ACD fines up to EUR 250,000, and forced re-registration or liquidation; under the proposed EU Unshell Directive the entity would be deemed non-resident and denied DTA protections
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the recaptured withholding tax and fines where they knowingly maintained a fictitious structure; they can be prohibited from serving as directors of any Luxembourg entity and may face bankruptcy liability for wrongful trading if the SARL continues operating without substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Participation Exemption Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing CAD/BIM services to the foreign shareholder at an off-market margin (e.g., using a 2% cost-plus rate while the ACD benchmark for engineering services is materially higher), concluding retroactive or sham service agreements, failing to file the Local File despite exceeding thresholds, or distributing dividends to a parent company before the 12-month holding period to obtain the 100% participation exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of the Luxembourg taxable base to the arm's-length profit, reassessment of municipal business tax and net wealth tax, 0.6% monthly late-payment interest, penalties up to 50% of the additional tax in cases of gross negligence or concealment, and denial of the participation exemption with immediate 15% WHT assessment on past distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed non-arm's-length agreements or premature dividend resolutions are personally liable for the additional assessment and penalties; criminal liability for complicity in tax evasion attaches if the TP manipulation was a deliberate mechanism to strip profits from Luxembourg

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cross-border wire and Wise payments from opaque clients without beneficial-ownership identification, processing payments that are inconsistent with genuine CAD/BIM deliverables, using the SARL as a pass-through for invoices unrelated to engineering work, or failing to maintain AML/KYC records under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 as amended
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF and Financial Intelligence Unit administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover per violation; criminal money laundering sanctions under Articles 506-1 to 506-8 of the Criminal Code carry imprisonment of 5 to 10 years in aggravated cases and fines up to EUR 5,000,000 for legal persons; the SARL's bank accounts may be frozen and the corporate license effectively revoked
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal prosecution with up to 10 years' imprisonment, confiscation of personal assets, travel bans, and mandatory disqualification from financial and commercial management functions; they are also subject to civil liability towards third-party victims and the State for the laundered amounts
